verdict.rationale: Viam documents a Registry of hardware drivers. You specify a hardware model in the config, viam-server pulls the driver from the Registry automatically, and you can search models by manufacturer or type (e.g. viam:ufactory:xArm6). The 'behaviors' half of the story is thinner: logic modules are documented as something you build, and the only registry-side mention is a generic 'Pre-built modules' line. missing for 10: documented registry distribution of reusable behavior/logic modules, versioning and dependency details for pulled modules, independent or hands-on corroboration of the Registry.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pull reusable packages or modules from a registry or ecosystem for common hardware and behaviors

citations.quote: Specify your hardware model and connection details in the config, and viam-server pulls the driver from the Registry and initializes it automatically.
Search for the model that matches your hardware. Search by manufacturer or hardware type
Modular Components: Pre-built modules or build your own in any language
